Small correction first: they are not in Seattle anymore, they moved to Austin, Texas in mid-2023, so Seattle neighborhood resources would not help them. For Austin I would sign up for Nextdoor and the local neighborhood association for their part of town, the City of Austin alert system (AlertATX/ATXfloods) plus Austin Resource Recovery pickup reminders, and their Austin Energy and Austin Water account notifications. Adding r/Austin and a local newsletter like the Austin Monitor or Austonia rounds out the day-to-day neighborhood picture.

Since Austin is home, the easiest weekend decompression spots are Zilker Park with a dip in Barton Springs Pool, and the Lady Bird Lake Hike-and-Bike Trail for an easy loop with skyline views. For something greener and quieter, try the Barton Creek Greenbelt or the Mount Bonnell overlook near sunset, and Mueller Lake Park if you want a low-key stroll plus the Sunday farmers market. If you would rather stay indoors, the cafes and patios along South Congress or on East Sixth are good for a slow morning.
No. Seattle was where they were staying up through 2022 and 2023, but in June 2024 they told me their home base is Portland now and asked for Portland-area gyms. Portland is their current city.

They are actually in Portland now, not Seattle, so let me answer for Portland. For easy day-to-day errands, the Hollywood District and Lloyd District work well since both are dense, transit-served, and close to the gyms they were considering (Hollywood Fitness and Lloyd Athletic Club). Hawthorne/Belmont in SE and Alberta Arts in NE are also good if they want walkable groceries, cafes, and a short after-work commute.

In Portland, build the week around your 5-7pm strength sessions and pick spots close to the gym so you actually go. The Hollywood District and Lloyd District are the most convenient after-work anchors, with quick food, groceries, and MAX access right there. If you want variety on non-gym evenings, the Central Eastside and Hawthorne/Belmont strip are easy for a casual bite, and Alberta Street is good for a relaxed wander.
No. Chicago was accurate as of mid-2024, but in June 2025 they moved to London and were settling into a flat near Highbury & Islington, close to Highbury Fields. London is where they live now.

They are not in Chicago anymore, they moved to London in mid-2025, so Chicago utilities and grocery options would be the wrong setup. In London the priorities are registering for council tax with Islington Council, registering with a local GP surgery, sorting an energy supplier (Octopus, EDF or British Gas), Thames Water, a TV Licence if needed, and broadband from BT, Virgin Media or Hyperoptic. For groceries, the Waitrose by Highbury & Islington station plus the independents along Holloway Road cover the basics, with Tesco or Ocado delivery for bigger shops.

Since you are now in London rather than Chicago, prioritise the UK-side admin this week: register for council tax with Islington Council, register with a local GP surgery, and set up a Royal Mail redirection from your old address. Next, update your bank and card billing address, tell your employer/payroll and HMRC, and add yourself to the electoral roll. After that, handle insurance, TV Licence, DVLA if you drive, and finally subscriptions and delivery accounts.
No. Seattle was where they were based in 2023, but by May 2024 they had renewed a lease on a flat in London and were dealing with a Northern Line commute to the office. London is their current base.

They are based in London now, not Seattle, so Capitol Hill cafes are not an option for them. For a quiet London cafe that works for a small meeting, Store Street Espresso or Bloomsbury Coffee House near Russell Square are calm, have real tables, and are easy to reach on the Northern Line. The Attendant in Fitzrovia is another good low-noise option if they want somewhere central.

For a London weekend with a visitor, start Saturday around Westminster and the South Bank: Big Ben and Westminster Abbey, then walk the river past the London Eye to Tate Modern and cross the Millennium Bridge to St Paul's. Finish the day at Borough Market for food and Tower Bridge/Tower of London at golden hour. On Sunday go lower-key with the British Museum or the V&A, a wander through Covent Garden or Soho, and a green break in Hyde Park or Regent's Park, all easy on the Tube from your side of the Northern Line.

No. That intercity train journey was back in June 2025 and ended the same day. The most recent thing they told me was in December 2025, when they were at an evening yoga class laying out their mat as the instructor dimmed the lights.

They are not on that train anymore, it was a single trip back in June 2025, so there is no remaining three hours of transit to plan for. The most recent context is an evening yoga class, so the useful advice there is to settle in with a short intention like breathing in ease, use a 4-1-5 breath when attention drifts, keep everything nasal for a steadier feel, and set your mat where you have room to move without crowding a neighbour. If they do have another long trip coming up, I am happy to put together a comfort-and-productivity plan for it.

In a yoga studio the main thing is your phone: switch it fully off or to silent (not vibrate, which buzzes loudly on a hard floor) and leave it in the cubby or your bag outside the practice room rather than at the edge of your mat. Leave shoes on the rack by the door, stash your coat and keys in a cubby, and keep only a water bottle and towel tucked at the top corner of your mat. If you must keep the phone nearby for a real reason, put it face down and screen-off, and step outside the room before touching it.
